title: Lamb Kofta
subtitle: Spiced minced lamb skewers with yoghurt sauce
excerpt: Minced lamb mixed with aromatic spices, shaped around flat metal skewers, and grilled over hot coals until the outside chars and the inside stays juicy. Served with flatbread, a cooling yoghurt sauce, and a sharp tomato salad.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kofta (from the Persian koftan, to grind or beat) are spiced ground meat preparations found across the Middle East, South Asia, and the Balkans in hundreds of variations. The minced-meat-on-a-skewer version, cooked over hot charcoal, is the most recognisable form internationally and is found from Morocco (kefta) to Turkey (köfte) to Iran (kabab koobideh) with regional variations in spicing and accompaniment. The key to a kofta that holds together on the skewer without falling apart is working the mixture very thoroughly until it becomes sticky and slightly tacky; under-worked kofta will slip off the skewer. Flat metal skewers are better than round ones; the flat surface gives the kofta more contact and prevents them rotating when turned.

content.text: The mince must have a reasonable fat content; very lean mince produces dry, crumbly kofta. Work the mixture with your hands for at least 3 minutes until it becomes sticky and holds its shape cleanly. Refrigerate the shaped kofta for 30 minutes before cooking; this helps them hold together on the grill.

items.preparation: very finely grated; moisture squeezed out

content.text: Combine the lamb, grated onion, garlic, all the spices, parsley, and salt in a large bowl. Work the mixture vigorously with your hands for 3 to 4 minutes until it becomes sticky and holds its shape. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Divide the mixture into 8 portions. Shape each around a flat metal skewer, pressing firmly to form an elongated sausage shape, or roll into cylinders if cooking in a pan. Make the yoghurt sauce by mixing the yoghurt, crushed garlic, and lemon juice. Season.

Grill over high heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side, or cook in a very hot griddle pan, turning a quarter-turn every 2 minutes, until charred outside and just cooked through. Serve with flatbread, yoghurt sauce, tomato salad, and pickled chillies.
